summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old man with a history of alcohol and opioid dependence, cirrhosis, and asthma was admitted for abdominal pain and alcohol withdrawal following a two-week relapse involving over a liter of hard liquor daily. He presented with tremors, nausea, vomiting, and an anion gap metabolic acidosis. CT imaging confirmed cirrhosis, portal hypertension, splenomegaly, and large varices, but ruled out pancreatitis. He was treated with a diazepam taper for withdrawal, IV fluids, thiamine, folate, multivitamins, and resumed PPI and H2 blocker therapy for gastric protection. His symptoms improved, withdrawal was managed without complications, and his liver enzymes and acidosis resolved. Suboxone was restarted on discharge. He expressed shame about his relapse but motivation to remain abstinent. He was discharged home with all prior medications continued and follow-up arranged with hepatology for liver monitoring and possible endoscopy.
problems: Acute alcoholic intoxication in alcoholism, unspecified
